Adds the 2024 Player's Handbook content the SRD 5.2.1 leaves out: the 12
backgrounds beyond Acolyte/Criminal/Sage/Soldier, and the 6 Origin feats
All 12 backgrounds were checked field by field against the Player's Handbook
(pages 179 to 185): ability scores, Origin feat, skill proficiencies, tool
proficiency and both equipment options. Acolyte, Criminal, Sage and Soldier
were re-checked too and match the SRD parse.
All descriptive prose here is original. The mechanics are game rules, which
are not copyrightable; none of the book's wording is reproduced.

feats.name: Crafter
feats.plain: You know three sets of artisan's tools, you buy gear cheaper, and you can make simple things quickly during a rest.

benefits.name: Tool Proficiency
benefits.text: You gain proficiency with three different Artisan's Tools of your choice.

benefits.name: Discount
benefits.text: Whenever you buy a nonmagical item, you get a 20 percent discount on it.

benefits.name: Fast Crafting
benefits.text: When you finish a Long Rest, you can craft one piece of gear from a list of options, provided you have the tools and the raw material cost.

choices.label: Pick three sets of Artisan's Tools

feats.name: Healer
feats.plain: You can patch someone up mid-fight with a Healer's Kit, no spell needed. Genuinely useful in a party with no cleric.

benefits.name: Battle Medic
benefits.text: As a Utilize action, you can expend one use of a Healer's Kit to restore Hit Points to a creature within 5 feet of yourself equal to 1d6 plus your Proficiency Bonus. A creature cannot benefit from this again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

benefits.name: Healing Rerolls
benefits.text: Whenever you roll a die to restore Hit Points with a spell or this feat, you can reroll the die if it rolls a 1, and you must use the new roll.

feats.name: Lucky
feats.plain: A pool of luck you spend to reroll with advantage, or to make an attacker roll badly. One of the strongest origin feats in the game.

benefits.name: Luck Points
benefits.text: You have a number of Luck Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus and can spend them as explained below. You regain your expended Luck Points when you finish a Long Rest.

benefits.name: Advantage
benefits.text: When you make a D20 Test, you can spend 1 Luck Point to give yourself Advantage on the roll.

benefits.name: Disadvantage
benefits.text: When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can spend 1 Luck Point to impose Disadvantage on that roll.

feats.name: Musician
feats.plain: Three instruments, plus you can hand out free rerolls to the whole party after a rest. Quietly excellent in a group.

benefits.name: Instrument Training
benefits.text: You gain proficiency with three Musical Instruments of your choice.

benefits.name: Encouraging Song
benefits.text: As you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can play a song on a Musical Instrument with which you have proficiency and give Heroic Inspiration to allies who hear the song. The number of allies you can affect equals your Proficiency Bonus.

feats.name: Tavern Brawler
feats.plain: Your fists actually hurt, you can shove people around, and you can fight with a chair leg. Fun and surprisingly effective.

benefits.name: Enhanced Unarmed Strike
benefits.text: When you hit with your Unarmed Strike and deal damage, you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to 1d4 plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike.

benefits.name: Damage Rerolls
benefits.text: Whenever you roll a damage die for your Unarmed Strike, you can reroll the die if it rolls a 1, and you must use the new roll.

benefits.name: Improvised Weaponry
benefits.text: You have proficiency with improvised weapons.

benefits.name: Push
benefits.text: When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can push the creature 5 feet away from yourself. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

feats.name: Tough
feats.plain: Two extra hit points now and two more at every level. The simplest way to stop dying at low levels.

benefits.name: Tough
benefits.text: Your Hit Point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a character level thereafter, your Hit Point maximum increases by an additional 2 Hit Points.

backgrounds.name: Artisan
backgrounds.tagline: You learned a trade. You can make and mend things nobody else can.
backgrounds.plain: Apprenticed to a smith, a potter, a glassblower or a jeweller. You know how things are built, which means you also know how they come apart.

tools.label: Choose one kind of Artisan's Tools

backgrounds.name: Charlatan
backgrounds.tagline: You sold something that did not work to someone who believed you.
backgrounds.plain: Fake potions, forged papers, a very convincing accent. You are good at being whoever the moment needs you to be.

backgrounds.name: Entertainer
backgrounds.tagline: You performed for crowds and learned to hold a room.
backgrounds.plain: Music, acrobatics, storytelling, or all three. You know how to read an audience and how to get out of a tavern quickly when the reading goes wrong.

backgrounds.name: Farmer
backgrounds.tagline: Hard work, early mornings, and more toughness than anyone expects.
backgrounds.plain: You grew up working land and minding animals. The Tough feat means you start with more hit points than any other background gives you.

backgrounds.name: Guard
backgrounds.tagline: You watched a gate or a wall, and you noticed everything.
backgrounds.plain: Long shifts on a city wall teach you to spot trouble early. Alert means you act sooner in a fight than almost anyone.

tools.label: Choose one kind of Gaming Set

backgrounds.name: Guide
backgrounds.tagline: You led people through country that would have killed them.
backgrounds.plain: Trails, weather, and which berries are safe. You come with two druid cantrips and a knack for not being seen.

backgrounds.name: Hermit
backgrounds.tagline: You lived alone and worked something out.
backgrounds.plain: Years away from people, tending to yourself. The Healer feat lets you patch up your friends without spending any magic at all.

backgrounds.name: Merchant
backgrounds.tagline: You bought low, sold high, and got lucky more than once.
backgrounds.plain: Caravans, ledgers and haggling. The Lucky feat gives you a pool of rerolls, which is one of the best things a level 1 character can have.

backgrounds.name: Noble
backgrounds.tagline: You were raised with money, manners and expectations.
backgrounds.plain: Titles, tutors and a family name that opens doors. People listen to you before you have said anything worth hearing.

tools.label: Choose one kind of Gaming Set

backgrounds.name: Sailor
backgrounds.tagline: You crewed a ship and won a lot of arguments with your fists.
backgrounds.plain: Rigging, storms and dockside brawls. Tavern Brawler turns your fists into a real weapon and lets you shove people around.

backgrounds.name: Scribe
backgrounds.tagline: You copied documents for a living and caught what others missed.
backgrounds.plain: Ink, patience and a very sharp eye. Scribes notice the detail in a contract, a map or a ransom note that everyone else skims past.

backgrounds.name: Wayfarer
backgrounds.tagline: You lived on the road and on the street, and you survived it.
backgrounds.plain: No fixed home and no safety net. You read people fast, you move quietly, and luck has a habit of finding you when it matters.
